extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for managing school classes: how to examine (recitation) and instruct groups efficiently, maintain discipline, stimulate interest, and foster pupil independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and minimize wasted instructional capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher should understand what is the full beneficial effect, which it is possible, in theory, to derive from his instructions, and recognize that to the extent he falls short there is waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of unused teaching power (analogy: 'a factory of a hundred spindles, with a water-wheel of power sufficient for a thousand'); plan to reduce waste by improving methods and 'machinery' of instruction as resources allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to both Recitation and Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects which are to be secured, in the management of classes, are twofold: 1. Recitation. 2. Instruction. These two objects are entirely distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not neglect either. Instruction includes explanation and assistance; recitation is the examination of individuals to ensure they have done assigned tasks. Balance explanatory teaching with reliable methods of examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfy yourself that the whole class is prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: The teacher must, in some way or other, satisfy himself, by reasonable evidence, that the whole class are really prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ingenuity to contrive means for examining the whole class in the shortest possible time; some individual examination is unnecessary daily if collective evidence of preparedness is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer methods that act on the whole rather than individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: A little machinery, a little ingenuity, in contriving ways of acting on the whole, rather than on individuals, will very much promote the teacher's designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: require all to write answers on slates and then read them together; use simultaneous response methods to test the entire class quickly and efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train classes in precise, simultaneous operations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is highly desirable that the classes should be trained to military precision and exactness in these manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, practiced commands (e.g., 'Prepare to write'), have pupils begin together, enforce exact obedience pleasantly but decisively to secure attention and speed; this increases engagement and allows mass handling of tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain firm but mild, good-humored discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Strictness of discipline is best introduced and maintained by a firm, but mild and good-humored authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sour looks and irritating language. Children respond well to pleasant but decided enforcement; discipline introduced ill-humoredly is unpopular and counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and manage excuses and unpreparedness collectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle excuses so as not to waste class time; do not permit constant individual interruptions when many are waiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set an agreed signal for those who wish to speak; announce that excuses will be heard at a set time; use group commands to separate prepared from unprepared; spend minimal time on each delinquency and reduce recurrence by steady application of principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simultaneous recitation with guarded rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous recitation (addressing a question to all the class to be answered by all together) is very advantageous but has attendant dangers that must be guarded against.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dangers and cautions: (1) some answer too eagerly — expose the motive and forbid early answers; (2) some defer to catch others' replies — discourage copying and insist on independent promptness; (3) some do not answer — detect these by lip motion and question them individually; (4) long answers produce confusion — shape questions to admit a single-word reply or require written replies/read in turn. Prevent a few bright pupils from answering for all by alternating with individual questioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vary examination methods: single, simultaneous, and written replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Three methods—single replies (individual), simultaneous answers, and written replies—each have distinct advantages and drawbacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single replies are rigorous but time-consuming; simultaneous answers engage many but risk superficiality; written replies are thorough and train writing but take more time. Use a mixture to secure benefits of each and maintain variety to sustain interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use majority agreement as quick evidence of correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: When the class answers in concert, the teacher may take down the figures given by the majority as the answer obtained by the majority: it is, undoubtedly right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismiss the majority promptly and examine only those who differ; trust that truth is consistent while individual errors often contradict each other. Spot-check slates as pupils pass to ensure fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not over-investigate each error or excuse
rubrics_metrics.description: If a scholar is unprepared or has made an incorrect answer, it is ordinarily a mere waste of time to search for the particular error in detail for each pupil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the pupil plainly the fact (e.g., 'It is no matter if you cannot [find the error]... you have made a mistake') and press for care in future. Reserve detailed examination for the few persistent or exceptional cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awaken and sustain interest with varied, attainable challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Make intellectual effort and acquiring knowledge pleasant by removing obstructions and offering new, varied modes of work that are within pupils' reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce novel exercises (e.g., parsing in writing with columns), predict faults to stimulate attention, and vary mechanical modes while pursuing a steady objective; tailor variety to age and maturity—advanced classes need less contrivance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect school studies to practical life and current events
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring out frequently the connection between studies and the practical business of life to awaken interest in the school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use general exercises to integrate History, Geography, Political Economy with topical local or national events; assign research and recitation relating to current issues to make learning relevant and motivating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach composition with practical, local, and clear subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign practical subjects (relating to school business or events around you) rather than moral essays or empty declamation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct pupils to obtain real arguments (e.g., from parents) and present them distinctly and simply. Emphasize clear description, legible writing, correct spelling, punctuation, and grammar so pieces can be read fluently and produce effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist pupils toward independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist your pupils in such a way as to lead them, as soon as possible, to do without assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gradually diminish oral help as pupils advance; teach them how to understand books and solve difficulties themselves so they continue learning after leaving the teacher's reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve steady pursuit of objectives while varying methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Variety should be confined to modes of pursuing a permanent and constant object; do not abandon an objective because pupils are momentarily tired of the mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., continue patient repetition to master simple addition while changing presentation (dictation, peer comparison, pen-and-ink practice, ingenious examples) to maintain interest without losing focus on the goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require neat, clear mechanical execution in written work
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanical aspects (clean slates, perpendicular lines, legible writing) matter and should be taught and expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out common mechanical faults before inspection; encourage pupils by protecting their reputation (e.g., by postponing first imperfect efforts) and incentivize better execution next time.
